    INITIAL BRIEF OF INTERVENORS THE MOSELEY GROUP AND MULTIPLE
                       FORMER PRO SE INTERVENORS

       Intervenors James Gregory Waller, Marilyn Moseley Waller, Arthur Kyle Moseley, David

Moseley (Moseley Group), W. Trent & Deanna Lea Barley, AH (“Bert”) Broad III, Stephen T.

Broad, Christina Broad Ramsey, Kolt Bunch, Dahlberg Estate – Alice Powell, Dahlberg Estate –

Carol Pilgrim, Trustee, Jordan Moore & Dalke Investments, LP, M. Rex & Kellie A. Emerson,

Micheal Gibbs, Joe Johanson, Mark & Regina Kyzer, Lundgren, Carlton/Carlton &

Marilyn/Marilyn-Robert Kreig Trust, Matt & Suzzette McBee, Archie Morris, R.A. Morris, T.K.

Morris, Brant Myers (leases from Bonnie Brotherton) Wanye-Kenneth Nowlin, Joe Don Pace;

Donna Phillips, Joanna Kaye Schackelford, Sharry Ware, John & Cheri Warriner, and Jared

Whitworth (leases from Teresa Weber). submit this Initial Brief.

       This Initial Brief will identify each of the issues in the Order of Referral and Preliminary

Order, although the Moseley Group has no comment on many of the issues.

       The Moseley Group supports selection of Route 894 or Route 487 and opposes Route 392,

based on cost, habitable-structure avoidance, environmental factors (including upland woodlands

and water resources), and safety/reliability risks associated with the U3 Colorado River crossing




                                                3
                                                 SUMMARY


         The transmission line routing factors are in PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B); the facts in each individual case determine the weight given to each factor. In

applying the factors in this case, Applicants identified a final group of six candidate routes, none

of which contained Link U31. The PUC Staff identified Route 487 as best meeting PURA and the

PUC’s regulations; it does not contain U3. It is compelling that each of these seven finalist routes

use Links K13-K51-K52-M112.

    A. U3 is not the only suitable Colorado River crossing.

         A handful of experts hired by J. Luther King, The Wulff family, and other large landowners

argued that only routes using Link U3 should be considered. The evidence showed they were

wrong.

         U3 crosses at an ecologically significant stream segment (ESSS)3; Link J22 (Route 894)

does not4. U3 crosses at USFWS critical habitat5; J22 and J11 (Route 487) do not6. For

approximately two miles, U3 parallels the Colorado River (within one-half mile)7; J22 has no

significant paralleling8. Only U3 crosses within the North-Central Prairies major land resource area

(MLRA)9, where most of the rainfall occurs during high-intensity convective thunderstorms10. U3’s

proximity to an existing transmission line in an area of high-intensity convective thunderstorms

those who rejected the notion that U3 was the only suitable crossing; they each concluded that

     B. Routes 894 and 487 outperform 392 on key factors.
         On key issues indicated by the facts of this case; such as cost, habitable structures, stream

crossings, avoiding upland woodlands, and minimizing the crossing of open waters; Routes 894

and 487 better satisfy PURA and PUC regulations.

         And 392 performs poorly on several other environmental factors. Route 392 has 324 stream

crossings20, higher than 487 (282)21 and 894 (291)22. Route 392 crosses 2,904 feet of upland

woodlands23; 487 and 894 cross zero24. Route 392 crosses 3,266 feet of open waters25, significantly

higher than 487 (2,487 feet26) and 894 (2,117 feet27).

         Link U3’s asserted benefits do not outweigh the demonstrated environmental, safety, and

cost advantages of Routes 894 and 487, which far better satisfy the statutory and rule criteria.

                               ISSUES FROM THE ORDER OF REFERRAL

           JOINT APPLICATION
           1.       Is the applicants’ joint application to amend its CCN adequate?? Does the

application contain an adequate number of reasonably differentiated alternative routes to conduct

a proper evaluation?

                    Moseley Group has no comment.

           NOTICE
           2.       Did the applicant provide notice of the application in accordance with 16 TAC §

22.52(a)(1), (2), and (3)?

                    Moseley Group has no comment.

           3.       Did the applicant provide notice of the public meeting in accordance with 16 TAC §

22.52(a)(4)?

                    Moseley Group has no comment.

           PUBLIC INPUT
           4.       What were the principal concerns expressed in the questionnaire responses received

at or after any public meetings held by the applicants regarding the proposed transmission

facilities?

                    The Applicants’ public outreach reflected community preferences to minimize

           impacts to residences, ranches, and aesthetics. The record does not show community-driven

           insistence on a U3 river crossing. Rather, that notion came from experts hired by a relatively

           small and well-financed group of intervenors. No route drew overwhelming support, and

           each route had at least one opponent28.



28
     PUC Ex. 1 (Poole Direct) at 40:9-11

            NEED
           5.       Taking into account the factors set out in the PURA § 37.056(c), are the proposed

transmission facilities necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the

public within the meaning of PURA § 37.056(a)?

                    Moseley Group has no comment.

           6.       In considering the need for additional service under PURA § 37.056(c)(2) for a

reliability transmission project, please address the historical load, forecasted load growth, and

additional load currently seeking interconnection.

                    Moseley Group has no comment.

           7.       Are the proposed transmission facilities the better option to meet this need when

compared to using distribution facilities? If' the applicant is not subject to the unbundling

requirements of PURA § 39.051, are the proposed transmission facilities the better option to meet

the need when compared to a combination of distribution facilities, distributed generation, and

energy efficiency?

                    Moseley Group has no comment.

           ROUTE
           8.       Weighing the factors set forth in PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B),

which proposed transmission-line route is the best alternative?

                    The route best meeting PURA and the PUC regulations is 894 or 487. They do well

           regarding the key criteria identified by Mr. Poole: cost, paralleling, avoiding upland

           woodlands, and habitable structures29.




29
     Id. at 64:14-65:5

         U3 is not the only suitable Colorado river crossing.
                 Routes 894 and 487 avoid U3’s negatives: crossing at an ESSS, crossing at USFW

        critical habitat, being within one mile of the Colorado River for approximately two miles,

        crossing at a significant river bend, and being in an MLRA where most of the rainfall occurs

        during high-intensity convective thunderstorms.

                 Those advocating U3 as the only suitable crossing of the Colorado River failed to

        analyze all the issues. While the “northern routes” were announced later in the process30,

        that delay did not prevent the PUC Staff, the Applicants, and several intervenor experts

        from identifying the multiple drawbacks of Route 392 and Link U3 in particular.

                 For example, while Mr. Sansom (a U3 proponent) acknowledged U3 is located in

        the Texas North Central Prairies MLRA, he did not know the application well enough to

        realize he was proposing a location where most of the rainfall occurred during “high-

        intensive convective thunderstorms.31” When asked if he was proposing to locate this

        transmission line next to an existing line in an area with high-intensive convective

        thunderstorms, he admitted he had no answer32. He did acknowledge that U3 will parallel

        the Colorado River and accepted that it will be for approximately 1-1.5 miles33.

                 The location of U3 is well depicted on Figures 6-L Panel 4 and Figure 6-14 from

        the application. Figure 6-14 shows that Link U3 will be within approximately one-half mile

        of the Colorado River for approximately 10,000 feet, or for almost two miles. Those

        advocating U3 ignored or minimized this risk, which is real34. Figure 6-14 shows U3 and

        the existing transmission line (red line with red dots) at essentially the same location.

        is so beneficial, only routes with U3 should be considered. Not only does this ignore the

        risks of locating two transmission lines so close to the river, it ignores the other

        environmental issues created by U3: crossing at an ecologically significant stream segment

        (ESSS)35; crossing at USFWS critical habitat36; crossing within the North-Central Prairies

        MLRA37 (where most of the rainfall occurs during high-intensity convective

        thunderstorms38); and crossing in an area with multiple river bends39.

         They also ignore the input from Texas Parks & Wildlife (TPWD). On March 21, 2025,

TPWD provided comments that recommended use of existing ROWs where practicable but also

recommended “crossing streams in a perpendicular manner and avoiding placement of lines parallel

to streams and their associated wooded corridors.40”

        The selected route should use Links K13-K51-K52-M11.

                 The PUC Staff views Route 487 as the route that best meets PURA and PUC

        regulations. The Applicants narrowed from 1,246 alternative routes to 122 alternative

        routes41 and then to 30 routes42 and finally to six43. All seven of these route finalists share

        the use of Links K13-K51-K52-M1144. They share these links because applying PURA and

        the PUC regulations leads to the conclusion that the route best meeting them will go through

        central McCulloch County approximately one-half mile south of the Brady city limits45.

                 These links impact several large and well financed landowners; they came together

        to hire multiple experts (and they led the charge in the unsuccessful appeal of the route

        adequacy decision).

                 Despite these experts’ qualifications, their evidence fell short. As discussed above,

        the evidence thoroughly discredited the notion that Link U3 was the only suitable Colorado

        River crossing.

                 Their other evidence in support of Route 392, which uses U3, was similarly

        unpersuasive. They argued that having the transmission line within the North-Central

        thunderstorms, would allow for lower construction and maintenance costs. Of course, none

        of the witnesses identified any mistake or failure to use acceptable methodologies when the

        Applicants estimated Route 392 costs of $2,110,686,000.00, compared to Route 894

        ($2,076,387,000.00) or Route 487 ($2,060,282,000.00)46.

                 Witnesses for these landowners made claims that the topography along Links K13-

        K51-K52-M11 made that area unsuitable for construction; they further characterized Route

        392 as encountering land more suitable, where construction would be more cost effective.

        None of them, expert or otherwise, could explain why these conclusions found no support

        in the Applicants’ cost estimates, which show Route 392 as more expensive than over 60%

        of the alternatives47.

                 From another perspective, Route 410 uses the same links as Route 894 through Link

        G51 and then it uses the same links as Route 39248. If Route 392 was indeed so economical,

        those savings should be shown in the Route 410 estimate. However, not only is 410 more

        expensive than 894, but it is also more expensive than Route 39249, suggesting a significant

        premium in costs for using 392, including Link H3, and avoiding Links K13-K51-K52-

        M11.

                 The experts hired by these landowners included Dr. Turnbough, who characterized

        the difference in habitable structures between Route 392 and Route 894 (a difference of 51

        structures over 225 miles) as numerically insignificant50. Just three weeks before, he called

            a difference of 105 structures over 365 miles (140 miles longer) a “large disparity51.” When

           asked about how he can characterize one as “numerically insignificant” and another as

           “large disparity,” he admitted: “There is no standard52.”

                       By acknowledging he developed an apparently “expert” opinion in the absence of a

           standard, he admitted his opinion is not credible evidence. When an expert cannot show

           how the opinion is derived from the data, the opinion is connected to the data only by the

           ipse dixit of the expert. It is of no help to the trier of fact. Gammill v. Jack Williams

           Chevrolet, Inc., 972 S.W.2d 713, 727 (Tex. 1998).

                       In summary, the evidence shows that Route 894 or Route 487 best complies with

           PURA and the PUC regulations.

           9.          Are there alternative routes or configurations of facilities that would have a less

negative effect on landowners? What would be the incremental cost of those routes or

configurations of facilities?

                       Based on comparative metrics for habitable structures, upland woodlands, stream

           and open-water crossings, and total cost, no alternative to Routes 894 or 487 would

           reduce overall adverse effects on landowners and environmental resources when weighed

           under the Commission’s multi-factor standard.

           10.         If alternative routes or configurations of facilities are considered because of

individual landowners' preferences, please address the following issues:

                       a.     Have the affected landowners made adequate contributions to offset any

           additional costs associated with the accommodations?

            COST TO CONSUMERS
            11.     Are the proposed transmission facilities necessary to meet state or federal reliability

standards?

                    Moseley Group has no comment.

            12.     What is the estimated cost of the proposed transmission facilities to consumers?

                    Cost remains a core factor in the Commission’s route selection analysis and on this

            record favors 487 and 894; the cost of Route 487 is $2,060,282,000.0053; the cost of Route

            894 is $2,076,387,000.0054.

                    Calls to disregard material cost differentials are inconsistent with the record and

            standard Commission practice in CCN routing. The analysis of the Applicants and the

            PUC Staff accords appropriate weight to relative costs alongside other factors.

            13.     What is the estimated congestion cost savings for consumers that may result from

the proposed transmission facilities considering both current and future expected congestion levels

and the ability of the proposed transmission facilities to reduce those congestion levels?

                    Moseley Group has no comment.

         BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES
        14.      Are the best management practices for construction and operating transmission

facilities that are standard in the Commission’s electric CCN orders adequate? If not, what

additional practices should be required for the proposed transmission facilities?

        The hearing produced extensive evidence of the best management practices (BMPs) the

applicants will incorporate to minimize negative impact. The Applicants’ witnesses gave

extensive testimony regarding their experience in applying BMPs in a variety of circumstances55.

The Applicants’ witnesses never said these BMPs were inadequate for any of the routes,

including Routes 894 and 487, which include Links K13-K51-K52-M11.

        15.      For each additional practice proposed, please address the following:

                          a.      What is the additional cost to design, construct and operate the

                 proposed transmission facilities, including the cost to consumers?

                          b.      What benefit, if any, will the proposed practice provide?

                          c.      What effect, if any, will the proposed practice have on the reliability

                 of the transmission system?

                          d.      What effect, if any, will the proposed practice have on the design,

                 construction, or operation of the proposed transmission facilities?

                          e.      What effect, if any, will the proposed practice have on the expected

                 date to energize the proposed transmission facilities?

         TEXAS PARKS AND WILDLIFE DEPARTMENT
        16.      Did the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department provide any recommendations or

informational comments regarding this application in accordance with section 12.0011(b) of the

Texas Parks and Wildlife Code? If so, how should the Commission respond through its order?

                 TPWD provided comments in a letter dated March 21, 202556. While TPWD

        roads, pipelines, transmission lines, or other utility rights-of way (ROW)…57,” TPWD

        also recommended, “crossing streams in a perpendicular manner and avoiding placement

        of lines parallel to streams and their associated wooded corridors58.”

                                                   SUMMARY


            The transmission line routing factors are in PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B); the facts in each individual case determine the weight given to each factor. In

applying the factors in this case, Applicants identified a final group of six candidate routes, none

of which contained Link U31. The PUC Staff identified Route 487 as best meeting PURA and the

PUC's regulations; it does not contain U3. It is compelling that each of these seven finalist routes

use Links K13-K51-K52-Ml 12.
